title: A split solvable group admits a faithful upper triangular representation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $H$ be a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Assume $H$ is split solvable [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]: there is a finite descending series of smooth connected closed $k$-subgroups, each normal in its predecessor, whose represented fppf quotients are $\mathbf G_a$ or $\mathbf G_m$, with $\mathbf G_a(A)=(A,+)$ and $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$. Then there are an integer $n\geq1$ and a closed immersion of $k$-group schemes $H\hookrightarrow B_n$, where $B_n$ is the subgroup scheme of $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] whose points over every commutative $k$-algebra are the invertible upper triangular matrices. Closed immersion has the meaning of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The trivial group is allowed, and no perfection or characteristic-zero assumption is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 16.52, forward implication, printed p.343, together with Proposition 16.2(a) implies (c), printed pp.324--325. Only the forward implication is used: its converse requires perfection.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation] to $H$. It gives $n\geq1$ and a closed group-scheme immersion $\rho:H\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$, injective on every algebra's points. Its hypotheses hold because $H$ is affine and finite type over the field $k$.

source.place: Proposition 16.52, first sentence, p.343; Theorem 4.9, p.87.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-complete-linear-flag-scheme], $X=\operatorname{Fl}_{n,k}$ is proper and finite type, with a scheme action of $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$. Restrict this action along $\rho$. The coordinate flag $k^i\times0^{n-i}$ is a $k$-point of $X$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-solvable-rational-fixed-point]: split solvability is assumed, and the required rational point has just been specified. Obtain a complete flag $0=V_0\subset\cdots\subset V_n=k^n$ such that $\rho_A(h)(V_i\otimes_k A)=V_i\otimes_k A$ for every $k$-algebra $A$ and $h\in H(A)$.

source.place: Proposition 16.52, p.343; Propositions 7.29--7.30, p.146, and Theorem 16.51, p.343.

proof.text: Choose $e_i\in V_i\setminus V_{i-1}$ successively. Since $\dim_kV_i=i$, induction gives $V_i=\langle e_1,\ldots,e_i\rangle$, so $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ is a basis. Let $P\in\operatorname{GL}_n(k)$ have these columns and set $\rho'=P^{-1}\rho P$. Over every $A$, preservation of $V_j\otimes_k A$ says that column $j$ of $\rho'_A(h)$ has zero entries in rows $i>j$. This uses all algebra-valued points, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Proposition 16.52 and the definition of a trigonalizable representation before Proposition 16.2, pp.324,343.

proof.text: Explicitly $B_n$ is the closed affine subscheme of $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ cut out by $x_{ij}=0$ for $i>j$, with coordinate algebra $k[x_{ij}:i\leq j][(\prod_i x_{ii})^{-1}]$. The below-diagonal coefficients of $\rho'$ vanish: evaluate the preceding universal assertion on the universal point $\operatorname{id}_H\in H(k[H])$. Thus the coordinate map factors through this quotient, giving a morphism $b:H\to B_n$. Upper triangular invertible matrices and their inverses preserve the coordinate flag, so $B_n$ is a finite-type affine group scheme; the group identities for $b$ follow from those for $\rho'$. The maps $b_A$ are injective since $P^{-1}\rho_A P$ is injective. Therefore [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-faithful-closed-immersion] makes $b$ a closed immersion. The construction also covers $H=1$ and $n=1$.

source.place: Proposition 16.2(b) implies (c), pp.324--325; Corollary 3.35, p.75; Proposition 16.52, p.343.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 16.52, forward implication, p.343, and Proposition 16.2(b) implies (c), pp.324--325.

Step 1: lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation needs only an affine finite-type group over a field, which H is. It gives a closed-immersion ρ that is injective on all A-points. Step 2: the new flag node gives a proper finite-type Fl_n with GL_n acting by g·F=gF; the action restricts along ρ, and the coordinate flag is a k-point. The new fixed-point node's hypotheses (split solvable, X proper, X(k)≠∅) all hold. Its universal fixedness is exactly ρ_A(h)(V_i⊗A)=V_i⊗A. Step 3 is the adapted basis, checked by hand. Step 4: GL_n/(x_ij, i>j) = k[x_ij : i≤j][1/∏x_ii]; the universal point gives the factorization b; and lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-faithful-closed-immersion (injective on all points ⇒ closed immersion) applies to H and B_n, both affine of finite type. Both new nodes are true and statement-only. The fixed-point theorem holds for nonreduced proper X via the valuative extension and separatedness, and agrees with the existing torus case. The flag scheme holds over any field. Neither new node restates the item. Not duplicates: lem-sfb-split-torus-rational-fixed-point (tori only), lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point (algebraically closed field), lem-sfb-solvable-subgroup-flag-realization (algebraically closed field), lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective (one Grassmannian), lem-sfb-lie-kolchin-triangular-embedding (algebraically closed field).
